quota_value.basis: List-price value of in-scope tokens divided by (weekly-window quota points used x fee per point), fee per point = monthly price x 7/30 / 100. Pooled across 5 accounts. Daily rows 2026-10-01..10-09, each covering the trailing 7 days. Excludes the 09-25/26 rows (85-88x), recorded before the series settled. Reads 1-2% high, because usage between the last reading and a reset is lost.
quota_value.token_mix: Agentic coding, 98.5% cache read, 1.3% cache write, 0.13% output, 0.07% reasoning, 0.01% input, over 44.9B tokens. A chat-heavy mix would read differently.

quota_value.refusal_reason: No Max 5x account is held, so astrocyte has measured none; the operator can state a figure.

prices.refusal_reason: "pro" is an API plan string, not a vendor tier name. OpenAI publishes Pro 100 ($100), Pro 200 ($200) and Pro 500 ($500); the API plan string does not establish which an account holds, so this key cannot carry one price. The tier rows are openai/pro_100, openai/pro_200 and openai/pro_500; the account's tier is a fact about the account.

quota_value.refusal_reason: Pro 100 is unmeasured: the one account possibly on it is not configured in astrocyte and its tier is unconfirmed.

quota_value.basis: List-price value of in-scope tokens divided by (weekly-window quota points used x fee per point), fee per point = monthly price x 7/30 / 100, each account's points weighted by its own fee. Codex weekly ('primary') window, daily rows 2026-09-25..10-09, each covering the trailing 7 days, recorded by astrocyte under the old key name pro_20x until 10-09. Rows 09-25..10-06 pool 2 accounts on $200 Pro 200 and read 28.8-40.9x. From 10-07 a third account on $100 Pro 100 is counted too, so those rows are a pooled Pro 200 + Pro 100 figure rather than a pure Pro 200 one, and read 25.1, 23.1 and 22.8x. The series is falling, from about 40x in late September to about 23x on 10-09, so the low end is the current reading. Per-account values cannot be separated, because harness tokens carry no account. Hand-checked over two weeks to within 2%; reads 1-2% high, because usage between the last reading and a reset is lost.

response.tier_vocabulary: The tier is the VENDOR'S OWN TIER NAME, never an API plan string. OpenAI's Pro 100, Pro 200 and Pro 500 are pro_100, pro_200 and pro_500 here. A consumer holding an API string must map it to a tier itself, with knowledge of the account.
response.unit_policy: US list price, monthly-billed, web subscription. An operator on an annual term, in another country, or subscribed through an app store pays something else, and this plane cannot see which.
